pinnedOracle.samePiCalibration: All six file-backed migration cases produced identical normalized records over two independent open/reopen runs.

pisharp.interchangeClassResult: 50/50 passed in the final PiJsonlSessionInterchangeTests class.

strictComparisons.v1LinearCompactionAndHookMessage: Generated IDs are linked in physical order, firstKeptEntryIndex maps past the session header, the index field is removed, the hook role becomes custom, and canonical export/reimport leaves entry records stable.
strictComparisons.v2HookMessage: Existing IDs and parent links are retained while hookMessage becomes custom.
strictComparisons.v3: Existing IDs and parent links remain stable; hookMessage is preserved because the version-3 file does not run legacy migration.
strictComparisons.v1InvalidCompactionFields: Pinned Pi deletes numeric firstKeptEntryIndex fields after attempting integer-index lookup, including zero, negative, out-of-range and fractional values; it preserves string, null and boolean values. PiSharp now matches this distinction. A numeric malformed timestamp and unknown field remain intact through migration and export.
strictComparisons.readOnlyFileBackedMigration: Pi migrates and rewrites v1/v2 files when opened. PiSharp LoadAsync migrates in memory and preserves original file bytes until an explicit guarded save.

acceptedDifferences.pinnedPi: The current pinned loader accepts a version-4 header and leaves its entries unchanged.
acceptedDifferences.piSharp: The importer rejects versions above 3 before constructing a canonical session.

acceptedDifferences.pinnedPi: The current loader accepts a string version "3" and does not migrate it because JavaScript numeric comparison coerces the value.
acceptedDifferences.piSharp: The importer requires an integer JSON number and rejects the header.
